verdict: Mechanics stay green (28/28 pages, 0 failed, 100% infobox, 0 hallucination, 0 junk, 48/48 typed relations) - every defect this run is a content-coverage defect, and they compound on the one page that matters most. Alice's page is written from chapters 7-11 only: extract_context string-sorts itemN keys and hard-breaks on the 8k budget, so the protagonist loses the first half of the novel (STU-711). Her arc then draws 18 events under a hardcoded cap that leaves chapters 2/5/10 unrepresented - no Caterpillar, no DRINK ME/EAT ME (STU-713) - and orders the ones it keeps by salience within each chapter, which is why the ch9 paragraph reads as three unrelated beats in reverse (STU-712). Underneath all of it, classify-relationships returns nothing on 48/48 pairs, so the event layer runs on one source instead of two (STU-700). Next action: STU-711 - a sort plus a budget policy, and the one that decides whether the protagonist's page is written from the whole book.
